units.summary: ParseQuantity now caches the canonical string on the returned Quantity in the two non-early return paths, since String() no longer caches. Parsed quantities keep their cached string for later encoding.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now caches canonical string before returning
units.reason: Changes what state parsed Quantity values carry (unexported s), affecting equality, encoding cost and data-race behavior across the API machinery.
focus: Every return path in ParseQuantity sets q.s (early '0' and canonical-input paths already did)
Callers that compare parsed Quantities with reflect.DeepEqual against constructed ones

units.summary: String() no longer writes the computed string back to the receiver; it returns the cached value if present, otherwise computes without caching. This removes a data race on concurrent reads but makes quantities built without ParseQuantity recompute on each call.
units.headline: Quantity.String no longer mutates receiver or caches result
units.reason: Removes a side effect of a widely used method, changing concurrency behavior and performance of encoding paths.
focus: Quantities created via NewQuantity/NewMilliQuantity/math ops now recompute String on each call in JSON/proto marshaling
Code or tests that relied on String() populating q.s (DeepEqual comparisons)

units.summary: Adds a new exported method that computes the canonical string and stores it on the receiver, for callers that own the instance. It always writes, so racy use is detected by the race detector.
units.headline: Add exported Quantity.CacheString that stores canonical string
units.reason: New public API method that mutates the receiver, with concurrency contract the caller must honor.
focus: Unconditional write q.s = q.String() on an already-cached instance can race for shared instances
Nil receiver returns "<nil>" consistent with String

units.summary: The test now asserts that ParseQuantity sets the cached string, replacing assertions that expected it to be empty after parse and set after String(). Expectations were changed to match the new behavior.
units.headline: TestQuantityString expects ParseQuantity to pre-cache string
units.reason: Test expectations were inverted to match new behavior, and an assertion about String() caching was removed.
risk_signals: expectations changed to match new behavior
focus: Removed check that String() populates q.s is intentional given String no longer mutates

units.summary: New test verifying CacheString returns and stores the canonical string, is idempotent, and handles a nil receiver.
units.headline: Add test for Quantity.CacheString
units.reason: New test only; cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: Benchmark rewritten to use sub-benchmarks per quantity and b.Loop; the Precalc variant was removed since String no longer caches. Benchmark-only change.
units.headline: Rewrite String benchmark as per-value sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark converted to per-value sub-benchmarks with b.Loop, forcing BinarySI format. Benchmark-only.
units.headline: BinarySI String benchmark uses sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark now iterates over the shared test cases as sub-benchmarks. Benchmark-only.
units.headline: ParseQuantity benchmark iterates shared testcases
